userStories.title: Store the fix ready result on a FIX job
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist and expose a FIX job's ready result without changing fixOutcome or verdict semantics.

**Motivation** — A FIX job records only `fixOutcome` (`pushed` / `nothing`) and `resultSha`.

**Approach** — The runner's `readFixState` reads `bot-state.json` once: `pushedSha` (40 hex), `markedReady` (boolean), `readyHeld` (string, clipped to 500 characters), `replied`, `resolved` (non-negative integers). `fixReady` is null when `markedReady` is absent; otherwise `{ markedReady, readyHeld?, replied?, resolved? }`. `judge` adds `fixReady` to the snapshot next to `fixOutcome`. The API's `mirror` keeps a `fixReady` whose `markedReady` is boolean, drops a non-string `readyHeld` and non-integer counts, clips `readyHeld` to 500.

**Scope** — In: API/protocol storage half of that design: add `FleetJob.fixReady Json?` through migration `20261122090000_fleet_job_fix_ready`; map JSON and Prisma.DbNull in repository reads/updates, domain record/patch and nullable DTO, retaining fixReady on list summaries. Reset it next to fixOutcome on requeue. Add the type-only protocol field and regenerate root OpenAPI and CLI client with `bun run generate`. Out: runner state-file reading and final snapshot production (US-002), ruling records and dispatch snapshots (US-003/US-006), ticket comments (US-009), web and CLI formatting (US-011/US-013).

**Interface** — `SnapshotEventPayload` target: `fixReady?: { markedReady: boolean; readyHeld?: string; replied?: number; resolved?: number }`. `FleetJobRecord` / `FleetJobPatch` target: `fixReady?: FixReady | null`. `FleetJobDto` gains `fixReady` (nullable). `mirror(p)` also maps a valid `p.fixReady` to the patch. Exercise the existing private mirror through `interpretEvent('snapshot', payload)`. Missing/invalid fixReady omits the patch field rather than clearing a prior value; optional counts are non-negative integers.

Use the existing event-payload, repository, DTO and requeue tests plus the new fix-ready unit spec; integration cases must round-trip real persisted snapshots, GET and requeue outside the sandbox.

[integration] After a FIX job's snapshot with fixReady: { markedReady: true } is applied, GET /projects/:slug/fleet/jobs/:id answers fixReady: { markedReady: true }.
[integration] GET /projects/:slug/fleet/jobs/:id of a RUN job answers fixReady: null.

userStories.title: Runner reads the fix ready result
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Read nax's FIX ready result once and report it with the existing FIX snapshot.

**Motivation** — A FIX job records only `fixOutcome` (`pushed` / `nothing`) and `resultSha`.

**Approach** — The runner's `readFixState` reads `bot-state.json` once: `pushedSha` (40 hex), `markedReady` (boolean), `readyHeld` (string, clipped to 500 characters), `replied`, `resolved` (non-negative integers). `fixReady` is null when `markedReady` is absent; otherwise `{ markedReady, readyHeld?, replied?, resolved? }`. `judge` adds `fixReady` to the snapshot next to `fixOutcome`. The API's `mirror` keeps a `fixReady` whose `markedReady` is boolean, drops a non-string `readyHeld` and non-integer counts, clips `readyHeld` to 500.

**Scope** — In: replace readPushedSha in verdict/fix-result.ts and callers with readFixState, carry fixReady in HostExecutor.readFixOutcome/job-executor and append a non-null value in JobRun.judge. Missing, unreadable, invalid JSON or symlink state is non-fatal and leaves outcome unchanged; absent markedReady yields no snapshot fixReady field. Preserve PR-specific stdout parsing, pushedSha validation, realpath containment, O_NOFOLLOW, single read and handle cleanup. Out: API persistence/reset (US-001), ruling files/argv/probe (US-008), client rendering (US-011/US-013).

**Interface** — `readFixState(logPath): Promise<FixState | null>` with `FixState { pushedSha: string | null; fixReady: FixReady | null }`; `FixOutcome` gains the optional `readonly fixReady?: FixReady | null`. `readPushedSha` is replaced, not left as a second state read.

Move existing readPushedSha tests to assert readFixState.pushedSha without changing their meaning. Add temp-file/symlink tests in fix-result.fix-ready.spec.ts, update the host-executor exact outcome for a state without ready fields to include fixReady:null, and extend JobRun snapshots only where the fake outcome reports ready fields. The exit code must never become the verdict source.

userStories.title: Ruling record, keyword parser and service
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add durable, auditable ruling records and one shared nax-compatible keyword parser and creation service.

**Motivation** — The user leaves most rulings to agents ("agent also is a member, they can rule it").

**Approach** — New model `FleetPrRuling { id, projectId, repoId, prNumber, jobId, itemId, itemKind, text, disposition, actorType, actorId, state, skipReason?, appliedJobId?, commentId?, approvalRequestId?, createdAt, updatedAt }`, `state` one of `pending`, `applied`, `skipped`, `replaced`, index `[repoId, prNumber, state]` and `[jobId, itemId]`. A new `apps/api/src/fleet/rulings/` module holds it (repository extends `AbstractPrismaRepository`, behind a DI token). `parseRulingText(text): { disposition: RulingDisposition; reason: string; sha?: string } | null` in `fleet/rulings/ruling-keyword.ts` mirrors nax's grammar on the first non-empty line: `fixed <7-40 hex>[ — | - | : reason]` -> `fixed`; `waive: <reason>` / `waived: <reason>` -> `waived`; `override:` / `overridden:` -> `overridden`; `confirm[: reason]` / `confirmed` -> `confirmed`; `verify[: reason]` / `verified` -> `verified`; case-insensitive. koda's evidence rule: `waived`, `overridden` and `confirmed` need a non-empty reason, so `parseRulingText('confirm')` is null.

Creation design: `FleetPrRulingsService.create(principal, slug, jobId, dto)`, which in one transaction marks the `pending` ruling of the same `(jobId, itemId)` `replaced`, inserts the new `pending` row (its `text` normalised to start at the first non-empty line, trimmed), records the audit entry (`fleet.job.rule`, summary `ruled <itemId>: <disposition>`). The ticket step is added to this transaction by US-005. For bare verified, the authoritative AC requires reason 'verified'.

**Scope** — In: migration `20261122090100_fleet_pr_rulings`, model with onDelete:Cascade job/project relations and back-relations, domain/token/repository/service/parser, FleetRulingsModule registration in FleetModule, and audit/normalization/replacement behavior. The service is the sole creation writer. Module reads jobs through its own Prisma-backed repository, never imports FleetJobsModule, so future Jobs/Ingest/Assistant imports are acyclic. Out: REST/permission/approval command (US-004), ticket/comment effects (US-005), FIX snapshot (US-006), assign placement (US-007) and result reconciliation (US-009). No keyword-per-item-kind rule: any keyword may rule any item kind, as for a writer's thread reply.

**Interface** — `parseRulingText(text): { disposition: RulingDisposition; reason: string; sha?: string } | null`; `FleetPrRulingsService.create(principal, slug, jobId, dto)`; the model fields and state/index contract above are the persisted interface. Keep multi-line evidence in stored text, but inspect only its first non-empty line to parse the disposition.

Co-locate parser/service and DB-free module-compilation unit tests; real repository integration tests must verify normalization, replacement and audit in PostgreSQL using the shared DB gate. Do not create a route or gate in this story.

userStories.title: Ruling routes and permission
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose project-scoped ruling create/list routes with permission checks and replay-safe approval execution.

**Motivation** — The user leaves most rulings to agents ("agent also is a member, they can rule it").

**Approach** — `POST /projects/:slug/fleet/jobs/:id/rulings` body `CreateRulingDto { itemId: string (1..64, `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$`); text: string (1..2000) }`, `@UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard, RequiresGuard)`, `@Requires('fleet.job.rule')` (guard level, so a caller without the key gets 403 before any job state is read), `@ApprovalGated()`. `FleetPrRulingsService.ruleTarget(projectId, jobId, dto)` runs before the gate, in this order: the job is in the project (else 404 `fleet.jobs`); it is a RUN whose `workflow.outcome` is `draft` and whose `resultPrUrl` gives a PR number through `prNumberFor` on a GitHub repo (else 409 `fleet.rulings.notDraft`); it is the latest RUN of that PR (`latestRunForPr`, below; else 409 `fleet.rulings.notLatest`); `itemId` is in `workflow.openItems` (else 404 `fleet.rulings.unknownItem`); `parseRulingText(text)` is not null (else 400 `ValidationAppException` naming `text`). Then `ApprovalRouteGate.run({ key: 'fleet.job.rule', variant: FLEET_RULING_ROUTE_VARIANTS.create, projectId, input: { slug, projectId, jobId, ruling: dto } })`; pending answers 202. The command's `run` re-runs `ruleTarget` (so an approval decided after the item's ruling was applied, the outcome changed or a newer RUN appeared fails with the same 404/409 and writes nothing), then calls `FleetPrRulingsService.create(principal, slug, jobId, dto)`, which in one transaction marks the `pending` ruling of the same `(jobId, itemId)` `replaced`, inserts the new `pending` row (its `text` normalised to start at the first non-empty line, trimmed), records the audit entry (`fleet.job.rule`, summary `ruled <itemId>: <disposition>`), and runs the ticket step (US-005). The route answers 201 with `FleetPrRulingDto`. `GET /projects/:slug/fleet/jobs/:id/rulings` (`fleet.job.read`) lists the job's rulings, newest first, every state. `FLEET_RULING_ROUTE_VARIANTS = { create: 'rest:fleet.job.rule' } as const` in `fleet-ruling-route.commands.ts`. `latestRunForPr(repoId, prNumber)` loads the repo's RUN jobs whose `resultPrUrl` ends with `/pull/<prNumber>`, newest `createdAt` first, and answers the first whose `resultPrUrl` gives that PR number through `prNumberFor`. A fifth pre-gate check refuses an item whose latest ruling is `applied` (409 `fleet.rulings.settled`): nax already settled it. `fleet.job.rule` is a new catalog key (scope project, inventory row `['project']`); the `fleet.job.*` glob grants it to developer, `*` to project-admin, admin and owner. Its derived approval is approvable, floor `none`, default `none`.

**Interface** — `CreateRulingDto { itemId: string (1..64, `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$`); text: string (1..2000) }`; `FleetPrRulingsService.ruleTarget(projectId, jobId, dto)`; `FLEET_RULING_ROUTE_VARIANTS = { create: 'rest:fleet.job.rule' } as const`; route input `{ slug, projectId, jobId, ruling: dto }`. Follow MemoryRouteCommands: register `routeCommand<Input, Result>({ key, variant, parse, run, toResult }, loader)` in an OnModuleInit provider, unique per (key,variant), approved execution as the requester.

**Scope** — In: controller/DTOs/route command, catalog/inventory, en/zh fleet.rulings.notDraft/notLatest/settled/unknownItem/invalidText, read-list tenancy, target checks and command revalidation, direct agent default and policy-driven human approval. Update role matrix to 226 cells, guarded-operation inventories to 130, endpoint e2e happy/invalid/list cases, and regenerate OpenAPI/CLI. Out: ticket creation/comment insertion (US-005 extends the existing create transaction), dispatch head snapshot and runner (US-006–US-008), assistant/tool/client adapters (US-010/US-012/US-013). No keyword-per-item-kind policy or additional ticket/comment permissions. Rulings on PRs that no koda RUN produced; the ruling route accepts only a RUN job with a draft workflow outcome. Legacy workflow drafts (published before nax 0.91.2, no item index) and pipeline-mode escalations (`finish-audit/`).

Use DB integration route tests for guard-before-state ordering, no approval request on target errors, requester attribution and stale approval failure with no writes; keep catalog derivation unit-level. Treat the applied check as the extra pre-gate check after the text-parse check, preserving the stated relative order of other checks.

userStories.title: Post every ruling on the work's ticket
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Atomically attach every ruling to an existing eligible work ticket or one newly created finish ticket.

**Motivation** — The user leaves most rulings to agents ("agent also is a member, they can rule it").

**Approach** — Inside the create transaction, `FleetJobTicketEffects.ensureFinishTicket(job, principal)` locks the RUN job row (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on `FleetJob`), then answers the oldest `FleetJobTicket` link's ticket that is not soft-deleted and not `CLOSED` or `REJECTED`, when one exists; otherwise it creates a TASK ticket titled `Finish draft PR #<n> (<feature>)` through `TicketsService.create` as the ruling's principal, moves it to `IN_PROGRESS` through `startForDispatch`, links it to the RUN with `FleetTicketsService.link`, and writes the fleet PR link with `upsertFleetPrLink`. Then `createRulingComment(ticketId, body, principal)` writes a `RULING` comment authored by the principal (`authorUserId` or `authorAgentId`), body `<itemId> (<itemKind>): <text>`, and its id is stored on the ruling. `TicketsService.create` inside the ruling transaction gets one number allocation attempt (`runWithTicketNumberRetry` does not retry inside a transaction), so a concurrent ticket creation that wins the number answers 409 and the ruling is not written; the caller retries. `fleet.job.rule` alone is enough to create the finish ticket and its comments (no `ticket.create` check), as `fleet.job.dispatch` already starts tickets through `startForDispatch`.

**Interface** — `CommentType` gains `RULING: 'RULING'`. `FleetJobTicketEffects.ensureFinishTicket(job, principal)`; `createRulingComment(ticketId, body, principal)`; `lockJobRow(jobId)`; existing `TicketsService.create(projectSlug, dto: CreateTicketDto, principal)`, `TicketTransitionsService.startForDispatch(projectSlug, ticketRef, principal)`, `FleetTicketsService.link(jobId, tickets: DispatchTicket[])`, `PrismaFleetTicketsRepository.upsertFleetPrLink({ ticketId, jobId, url, provider, prNumber, externalRef, now })`.

**Scope** — In: add RULING enum/response contract, extend the US-003 create transaction with ticket selection/creation/start/link/comment and commentId, add repository row lock and authored comment insertion, append TicketsService and FleetTicketsService as the last constructor arguments of FleetJobTicketEffects, update its six positional unit fixtures, and name ensureFinishTicket as the second allowed startForDispatch caller in its doc comment. Regenerate OpenAPI/CLI for comment type. Out: ruling route/permission (US-004), runner results and system summaries/ready comments (US-009), web pill/edit control (US-011). `RULING` comments are immutable against edits only; deleting one is allowed and leaves the ruling's `commentId` pointing at a deleted comment. No ticket status change when a PR is marked ready, and no new ticket transition; the existing PR-merge sync moves the ticket.

New ticket effects must not use the surrounding class's old after-commit, best-effort error swallowing: any ticket/comment failure aborts the ruling transaction. Oldest means link age, not ticket number. Lock before eligible-ticket selection to serialize concurrent first rulings. Use real DB integration rollback/concurrency/merge tests and unit conflict propagation; keep unrelated effect assertions unchanged.

userStories.title: Snapshot the pending rulings at FIX dispatch
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Bind an explicitly dispatched FIX to the latest RUN's pending rulings and the PR head read at dispatch.

**Motivation** — The user leaves most rulings to agents ("agent also is a member, they can rule it").

**Approach** — At FIX dispatch, after the `reviewDecisions` snapshot and before the insert transaction, `FleetPrRulingsService.snapshotForFix(repo, prNumber)` selects the `pending` rulings of `latestRunForPr(repo.id, prNumber)`. With none it answers undefined and the job carries no `prRulings`. With some it mints a read-only token and calls `getPullRequest`; an open PR with a `headSha` gives `{ headSha, rulings: [...] }`, each ruling as `{ rulingId, item: itemId, ruling: text, by, at: createdAt ISO }`, at most 100 (the oldest `createdAt` first; the rest wait for the next FIX, since nax refuses a file of more than 100); a closed or missing PR gives `{ notSent: 'pr-not-open' }`; a thrown read gives `{ notSent: 'head-unreadable' }`. `by` is `koda:agent:<agent slug>` or `koda:user:<user name>`, newlines removed, clipped to 100 characters. userStories.title: Record what nax did with the rulings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Reconcile only the rulings sent by a FIX and report their durable outcomes and ready result on the work's tickets.

**Motivation** — A FIX job records only `fixOutcome` (`pushed` / `nothing`) and `resultSha`.

**Approach** — `parseBotReview` reads `callerRulings` from the selected artifact when present (each `applied` entry needs string `item` and `disposition`, each `skipped` entry string `item` and `reason`; malformed entries are dropped; `ignored` kept only when it is `untrusted-pr` or `head-mismatch`). In the FIX branch of `BundleIngestService.write`, `FleetPrRulingsService.recordResults(job, parse)` maps each item of `job.prRulings.rulings` to its ruling: an item in `applied` -> `applied`; an item in `skipped` with reason `echo-failed` or `recorder-failed` -> stays `pending`; any other `skipped` reason -> `skipped` with that `skipReason`; `ignored: 'untrusted-pr'` -> every sent ruling `skipped` with `untrusted-pr`; `ignored: 'head-mismatch'` or a missing `callerRulings` -> every sent ruling stays `pending`. Only rulings still `pending` change state. Each changed ruling gets `appliedJobId`. When at least one ruling changed, one system `RULING` comment is written on the RUN's ticket: `Finish <jobId>: applied D-1 (confirmed), B3 (waived); skipped G-1 (superseded-by-writer)`. When the FIX's `fixReady.markedReady` is true, one system comment `PR #<n> marked ready by FIX <jobId>` is written on the ticket of every RUN of the same repo whose `resultPrUrl` is that PR; ticket status does not change. Both system comments carry the FIX job id in their body, and each is skipped when the ticket already has a comment with exactly that body, so a re-delivered bundle writes neither twice. Ingest claims a bundle only after the job is terminal (`claimNext`), and the terminal transition follows the runner's final snapshot (with `fixReady`), so ingest sees `fixReady`.

**Interface** — `BotReviewParse` done variant gains `callerRulings?: { applied: { item: string; disposition: string }[]; skipped: { item: string; reason: string }[]; ignored?: 'untrusted-pr' | 'head-mismatch' }`. `FleetPrRulingsService.recordResults(job, parse)`. `PrismaFleetTicketsRepository.createSystemComment(ticketId, body)` takes an optional comment type (default `GENERAL`) so the summary is a `RULING` comment.

**Scope** — In: optional artifact parsing without changing old done results, conditional pending state updates through snapshot rulingId, appliedJobId/skipReason, transactional FIX ingest for COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED with existing epoch fencing, exact-body deduplicated summary/marked-ready comments, optional system-comment type, fixture stub updates. Out: ruling creation/ticket bootstrap (US-003/US-005), dispatch snapshot (US-006), runner parsing/echo behavior (US-008), web and CLI displays (US-011–US-013). No sweeper for `pending` rulings on PRs readied, merged or closed outside koda. No ticket status change when a PR is marked ready, and no new ticket transition; the existing PR-merge sync moves the ticket. K3's follow-up REVIEW after a pushed FIX is unchanged; replacing it with nax's own post-push re-review is a separate decision.

userStories.title: Web shows the fix ready result and ruling comments
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Show FIX readiness and thread reply counts on the job page and visibly immutable ruling comments on tickets.

**Motivation** — A FIX job records only `fixOutcome` (`pushed` / `nothing`) and `resultSha`.

**Approach** — FIX job page ready line and reply counts; `CommentThread` renders `RULING` with a label and no edit control. `FleetJobDto` gains `fixReady` (nullable). The FIX outcome line gains the ready result and reply counts. The comment type union and pill map gain `RULING`.

**Interface** — `fixReady?: { markedReady: boolean; readyHeld?: string; replied?: number; resolved?: number }` is the result shape; the web DTO exposes its nullable value. Locale keys `fleet.fixReady.*` and `comments.types.RULING` are added to both en.json and zh.json. True means translated marked-ready plus present reply/resolved counts; false means translated held followed by the raw reason. Only FIX jobs render this line, and null renders none.

**Scope** — In: job-page ready display, web fleet-types.ts field, CommentThread type/pill/edit visibility, English/Chinese copy, fix-ready page spec and existing job-detail fixture fixReady:null. Out: backend snapshot/persistence (US-001/US-002), server comment immutability (US-005), ruling form/Finish action (US-012) and CLI formatting (US-013). `RULING` comments are immutable against edits only; deleting one is allowed and leaves the ruling's `commentId` pointing at a deleted comment. No ticket status change when a PR is marked ready, and no new ticket transition; the existing PR-merge sync moves the ticket.

Use existing Jest SFC mount harness and job/comment fixtures. Keep pushed/nothing outcome text unchanged. Render readyHeld and other runner strings with Vue interpolation only, never v-html; use existing tokens for the new pill. This is an informational rendering change, not a new backend authorization policy.

userStories.title: Web open items, rulings and Finish
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Provide a draft RUN's open-item ruling UI and an explicit Finish dispatch for its GitHub PR.

**Motivation** — The user leaves most rulings to agents ("agent also is a member, they can rule it").

**Approach** — Open items table on a draft RUN with each item's latest ruling, a ruling form per row (`fleet.job.rule`), a Finish button (`fleet.job.dispatch`) that dispatches a FIX for the PR, and the `bot_rulings` misfit label. The tools, the web form and the CLI reach `FleetPrRulingsService` through the ruling route or the route command; none re-implements `parseRulingText`. The web reads `fixReady`, the rulings list and the misfit reason from the API DTOs.

**Interface** — `useFleetRulings(slug).list(jobId)` calls `GET /projects/:slug/fleet/jobs/:id/rulings`; `useFleetRulings(slug).create(jobId, { itemId, text })` calls `POST /projects/:slug/fleet/jobs/:id/rulings`. Both use `useApi()`/apiPath and existing envelope unwrapping. There is no existing web approval-pending interceptor: a 202 is a successful `{ ret: 0, data: <approval request summary> }`, and useApi returns only its data. Type create's result as the ruling-or-approval-summary union and recognize the summary's permissionKey/status before displaying success; a summary with permissionKey fleet.job.rule and status pending triggers the pending-approval toast. Keep ordinary list/create calls through useApi without direct fetch or duplicate server validation. `CreateRulingDto { itemId: string (1..64, `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$`); text: string (1..2000) }`; add `FleetPrRulingDto` to lib/fleet-types.ts and `bot_rulings` to the misfit union. `useFleetJobs(slug).dispatch` receives `command: 'FIX'`, `prNumber` and the current job's repo through the existing dispatch body, including required numeric maxCostUsd from the current job's configured cap; DispatchBody and DispatchFleetJobDto require that field, so the button must not submit only command/repo/prNumber. A form choosing waive and reason out of scope sends `text: 'waive: out of scope'`; confirm without evidence shows translated validation before a call. The API remains the full grammar authority.

**Scope** — In: FleetJobOpenItems.vue, useFleetRulings.ts, draft-RUN page integration, row id/kind/issue/file:line/latest ruling/ruler/state/skip reason, permission-controlled forms and Finish button, pending-approval toast, extractApiError on conflict, en/zh fleet.rulings.* and fleet.misfit.bot_rulings, workflow-page fixture updates and full new ruling state/skip-reason enum parity pins. Out: shared server validation/approval engine (US-004), snapshots/placement (US-006/US-007), runner settlement (US-008/US-009), ready result line/comment pill (US-011). US-012 only: the Finish button is not hidden after a PR is marked ready; a further FIX on a ready PR answers `nothing to fix`. GitLab: rulings and Finish are GitHub-only, like K1-K3.

Use project permission hints for visibility but rely on API guards for authorization. Render a separate draft-RUN panel without modifying the existing completed-REVIEW Fix link or PLAN Dispatch run handoff pinned by fleet-job-fix-action.spec.ts. Use the API DTO/list to determine latest ruling per item, show skipped reasons, and preserve safe interpolation and SSR-compatible composables. Test form/network/status behavior with Jest component/composable mounts and use the existing locale parity conventions.

userStories.title: CLI ready result and ruling commands
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose FIX readiness and ruling list/create operations through thin generated-client CLI commands.

**Motivation** — A FIX job records only `fixOutcome` (`pushed` / `nothing`) and `resultSha`.

**Approach** — `koda fleet job show` prints the ready result; `koda fleet job rulings <jobId>` lists rulings; `koda fleet job rule <jobId> <itemId> <text>` records one. API or network error, invalid option: shared `handleApiError`: 401/403 exit 2, 400 exit 3, 404 exit 4, other exit 1, approval pending exit 5; an invalid option exits 3 before any call. The tools, the web form and the CLI reach `FleetPrRulingsService` through the ruling route or the route command; none re-implements `parseRulingText`.

**Interface** — `koda fleet job rulings <jobId> [--json]` prints item/disposition/state/actor/skip reason or the unwrapped JSON list. `koda fleet job rule <jobId> <itemId> <text>` uses the generated create-ruling client with `{ itemId, text }`, prints the ruling id on success, and prints the approval request id with exit 5 on 202. FIX `showRows` adds `Ready`: `marked ready (replied 2, resolved 1)` or `kept as draft: CI failure: x` for the stated examples; RUN has no Ready row. Retain existing --project/context and JSON conventions.

**Scope** — In: new fleet-job-rulings.ts registration and Jest spec, FIX-only showRows Ready output, generated client calls, existing unwrap/withContext/handleApiError usage, local empty-text/invalid-option validation before API calls, existing fleet-job.spec.ts closed-world row updates only for FIX. Out: API grammar/permissions/approval implementation (US-003/US-004), ready persistence/runner (US-001/US-002), web form/Finish (US-012). Do not add handwritten HTTP or duplicate ruling business rules, and never hand-edit generated client code.

Mock generated functions at command boundaries and capture stdout/stderr/process.exit. Keep API messages on stderr and successful JSON on stdout through shared helpers. Regenerated client/DTOs are produced upstream by API contract stories; use their generated operation names rather than inventing independent endpoint wiring.

outOfScope: Settling workflow items any other way than nax's ruling path: no `nax workflow record` or `promote`, no writes to nax files, no koda-side GitHub thread replies.
Legacy workflow drafts (published before nax 0.91.2, no item index) and pipeline-mode escalations (`finish-audit/`).
Rulings on PRs that no koda RUN produced; the ruling route accepts only a RUN job with a draft workflow outcome.
No koda-side LLM drafts rulings; the ruler is whoever calls the route (a person, or an agent through MCP or CLI).
No automatic Finish: only an explicit FIX dispatch carries rulings; a REVIEW (manual or the auto-review poller) never carries rulings.
No keyword-per-item-kind rule: any keyword may rule any item kind, as for a writer's thread reply.
`fleet.job.rule` alone creates the finish ticket and its `RULING` comments; no `ticket.create` or `comment.create` check is added on that path.
US-007 only: the dashboard attention list does not surface a FIX waiting on `bot_rulings` as unplaceable (its queued rows carry no `prRulings`); the job's own misfit shows it.
US-012 only: the Finish button is not hidden after a PR is marked ready; a further FIX on a ready PR answers `nothing to fix`.
`RULING` comments are immutable against edits only; deleting one is allowed and leaves the ruling's `commentId` pointing at a deleted comment.
No sweeper for `pending` rulings on PRs readied, merged or closed outside koda.
No ticket status change when a PR is marked ready, and no new ticket transition; the existing PR-merge sync moves the ticket.
Red CI, merge conflicts and gate repair are not handled by Finish; they show as the fix ready hold.
GitLab: rulings and Finish are GitHub-only, like K1-K3.
K3's follow-up REVIEW after a pushed FIX is unchanged; replacing it with nax's own post-push re-review is a separate decision.
No PR head binding at ruling time: the head is read when the FIX is dispatched, and a push between dispatch and the review leaves the rulings `pending` (nax `head-mismatch`).
